October 4, 2026

Epstein whistleblower who exposed Lutnick ties dies by suicide

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

Simon Andriesz, a former British banker who reported Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's business association with Jeffrey Epstein, has died by suicide, according to reporting confirmed by the founder of the campaign group Transparency Task Force. Andriesz previously served as a managing director at BGC Group, where Lutnick was chief executive, and told the BBC he had unearthed evidence that Lutnick failed to disclose the relationship. One account from someone close to him said he had been in and out of mental health institutions for years while pursuing the case, and that the FBI never acted on his report.

Mass shooting at Georgia homecoming block party kills two, injures dozens

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A shooting at a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, at about 1:20 a.m. local time killed two people and injured as many as 35 others. Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavey said more than 25 people were taken to hospital. According to the Gun Violence Archive, there have been more than 350 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, more than the number of days elapsed.

House Republicans in triage as Trump tells voters to pretend he is on the ballot

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

With one month until election day, House Republicans have privately acknowledged that holding the chamber is likely impossible. Campaigning in Ohio, President Trump urged voters who dislike Senate and gubernatorial candidates Vivek Ramaswamy and Jon Husted to close their eyes and vote as though they were voting for him. Republican support is reported to be eroding in states including Alabama, Oklahoma and Ohio, all of which Trump carried by double digits.

Trump tells Ohio voters he will be less inclined to help if Democrats win

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

At a rally in Ohio, President Trump told voters that if they put Democrats in office he would be less inclined to help the state. The remark came alongside his promotion of direct payments to voters. He linked future federal assistance for the state to the election of his chosen candidates in November.

Trump declines to endorse Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

In a 75-minute interview with Time magazine published Thursday, President Trump deflected repeated questions on whether Israelis should return Benjamin Netanyahu to office ahead of the Oct. 27 vote, saying he is not involved in politics anymore. The election is the first national vote in Israel since the 2023 Hamas attack, and Netanyahu has campaigned on his relationship with Trump. Netanyahu also faces a long-running corruption trial, fallout from his 2023 judicial overhaul plan and criticism of security failures before Oct. 7. The seven-month Iran war has strained the relationship, with Trump objecting to an Israeli strike on an Iranian gas field and calling Netanyahu "crazy" in June over stalled peace talks.

DHS bought five planes from a donor for over $100 million and left them idle

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times reported that hours before Kristi Noem left her job, her agency purchased five aircraft from a donor at a significant markup, spending more than $100 million. The planes were intended to carry deportees but have largely remained idle, with most having flown no deportation flights. The purchase was the kind of spending the Department of Government Efficiency was created to eliminate.

Trump administration moves to strip road protections from 45 million acres of national forest

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Trump administration is seeking to repeal the 2001 roadless rule, which has kept new roads and logging out of 45 million acres of national forest, including about 4 million acres in Utah. The administration has framed the repeal as wildfire prevention, though the existing rule already permits crews to thin trees and fight fires, and fires are four times more likely to start near a road. The timber industry has been among the loudest voices pushing for the repeal. Public comments close Tuesday at 9 p.m. Utah time; polling cited indicates three out of four voters, including most Republicans, want the rule kept.

Arizona court throws out manslaughter sentence over AI video of victim

tags: legal, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The Arizona Court of Appeals has vacated a 10-year manslaughter sentence after the trial judge considered an AI-generated video depicting the deceased victim addressing the court. The victim's family created the video using his likeness to give him a voice at sentencing. The appeals court found the video violated the defendant's due process rights because it did not convey statements actually made by the victim, and ordered a re-sentencing. It is the first known use of an AI-generated video of a victim at a sentencing hearing.

District attorney declined to review additional Cornell evidence

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times confirmed that in 2024 Cornell police informed the New York district attorney reviewing the case against seven fraternity members that investigators had conducted additional interviews beyond the Jane Doe statement. Prosecutors said the statement was all they would review and declined to pursue charges or present evidence to a grand jury. New York Attorney General Letitia James has since been appointed special prosecutor over the investigation.

Cornell Jane Doe reports threats and pressure to drop lawsuit

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The woman suing Cornell University and seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity says she has received significant threats and pressure to drop the case, according to her lawyer. The attorney described repeated attempts to unmask her identity and said other women who are not the plaintiff have also been targeted. She has refused to withdraw the suit.

Iowa Republican avoids constituents asking about Epstein files

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa was filmed walking away from constituents confronting her over her refusal to back the release of the Epstein files. She has not signed the discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act, nor a second discharge petition on the matter. She is running in one of the closest House races in the country.

White House monitoring suspected plague outbreak in Siberia

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration is aware of and monitoring a suspected plague outbreak in Siberia and assessing its options, according to Axios. Russian health authorities quarantined nearly 200 people who had contact with a woman who worked at an anti-plague research facility and later died; several hospitals are under quarantine and some universities are reported to be considering cancelling classes. Russian media reports the woman is suspected to have died of pneumonic plague, though health authorities have not confirmed the diagnosis. There is no indication of further spread at this time.

Trump says Obama more corrupt than Nixon as DOJ revisits Watergate

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump posted on Truth Social that former President Barack Obama is more corrupt than Richard Nixon. The claim comes as Trump's Justice Department seeks to recast Watergate, arguing Nixon was railroaded and the scandal was a setup. Trump is the only one of the three presidents to have been convicted of a criminal offence; Nixon was pardoned before any charges.

Trump discusses aspirin dose and calls data center opposition a Chinese psyop

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

At a rally in Ohio, President Trump said he takes a far larger daily aspirin dose than his doctors recommend, describing a prescribed dose in the 80-milligram range against the roughly 300-milligram dose he takes, and saying he needs it psychologically. He also claimed to know more about inflation than anyone else and singled out a woman in the audience as a housewife with a natural instinct for business. The crowd went quiet when he suggested that opposition to data centers is a Chinese psychological operation.

Newsom puts $7.5 billion science research bond on 2028 ballot

tags: politics, health, climate
sources: @groundnews

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a bill placing a $7.5 billion bond measure on the March 2028 ballot to create the California Foundation for Science and Health Research. The agency would issue grants and loans for public health, climate science and agricultural research. The measure follows federal research cuts, including nearly $2 billion in cancelled University of California grants beginning in 2025 that a court later largely restored, and is a scaled-down version of an earlier $23 billion plan that failed to reach the ballot.

Algeria makes forest arson punishable by death after wildfire surge

tags: legal, climate
sources: @groundnews

Algeria's national assembly passed a bill on Thursday making arson of forests or fields punishable by death, following more than 100 fires in the northeast during a North African heatwave. Civil Protection recorded 3,719 wildfires between May 1 and July 20, up from 1,501 in the same period of 2025. Justice Minister Lotfi Boudjemaa told parliament the death penalty was the appropriate response, said arson had reached the level of organised crime and claimed investigations pointed to ties with foreign parties. Algeria retains capital punishment in its penal code but has carried out no execution since 1993; the bill also extends the death penalty to child kidnappings involving torture, sexual assault or mutilation.

Singapore launches state matchmaking service as births hit 60-year low

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Singapore has launched FirstDate, a state-run matchmaking service open to government employees aged 21 to 35, as the country faces a record-low fertility rate. Users log in through the national digital identity system, complete a survey and are paired one date at a time using the Gale-Shapley stable marriage algorithm. Fewer than 30,000 babies were born in Singapore in 2025, the lowest figure in 60 years, with the total fertility rate falling to 0.87 from 0.97 in 2024, well below the 2.1 replacement rate. Critics online say the pilot discriminates against non-government workers and that its age cap shows it is aimed at raising births rather than helping people find partners.
